pages.title: Automatic Mating
pages.text: Domesticated animals mate automatically!$(br2)When a domesticated female and male are both well fed (at least 80% hunger) and the female is not in post-birth cooldown, she will approach the male to mate, and only then can she become pregnant.$(br2)The male must also be $(bold)domesticated, well fed and off cooldown$() - a wild bull will not do.

pages.title: Pregnancy & Birth
pages.text: Pregnancy lasts about 120 minutes for cows (scaled by body size). Pregnant animals eat 1.5x faster and their belly grows bigger.$(br2)When the time comes, live-bearing animals give birth to a baby that is $(bold)domesticated from birth$().$(br2)That baby will not grow up on its own like in vanilla - a domesticated baby must be kept well fed. See $(l:animalflee:growth/growth_overview)Raising Young$().

pages.title: Oviparous Animals
pages.text: Oviparous animals (like chickens) do NOT get pregnant! They lay eggs on a fixed cycle.$(br2)A female lays an egg about every 1 MC day. Only eggs laid by a $(bold)domesticated female that has mated$() are fertilized; all others are normal eggs, and $(bold)wild oviparous animals only lay normal eggs$().$(br2)To hatch a chick, tame the hen first and let a rooster mate with her.

Keep your cows well-fed and a bull nearby. A pregnant cow that takes damage has a chance to miscarry, so protect her!$(br2)Horses and donkeys can also pair up and produce a mule.$(br2)Other mods that change breeding results - twins, breeding bonuses and the like - apply to babies born here and to chicks hatched here too.
